title: Hybrid accelerator integration and fidelity guidelines
author: Priya Nambiar
body:
Summary
This document defines the integration contract, quality/fidelity guidelines, and operational runbook for bringing hybrid accelerator resources (on-host GPUs + third‑party accelerators such as NPUs/DPUs/TPUs via remote attach) into Redwood’s serving runtime. It covers compatibility decisions, kernel-scheduling boundaries, profiling and benchmark requirements, preflight checks, rollout criteria, and rollback gates. The goal is to enable safe, measurable performance improvements while preserving inference fidelity and SLOs.

Scope and audience
- Scope: hybrid accelerator attachments that extend the runtime’s kernel execution layer (e.g., hardware with different numeric formats or reduced FP precision, remote-attached inference ASICs).
- Audience: runtime engineers, kernel scheduling owners, platform SREs, profiling engineers, and release engineers who validate new accelerator integrations.

Goals and design principles
1) Safety-first: no automatic traffic routing to a new accelerator variant without passing fidelity & stability gates.
2) Observable fidelity: every accelerator variant must emit a fidelity profile and regression signals tied to canonical prompt sets.
3) Isolated scheduling: scheduler must treat hybrid accelerator pools as distinct resource classes with explicit mapping rules.
4) Deterministic fallbacks: runtime must be able to fall back to a verified CPU/GPU kernel variant with bounded latency and output drift.

Definitions
- Accelerator variant: a compiled kernel implementation or model quantization that executes on a particular accelerator type/version.
- Fidelity profile: per-model/per-prompt metrics comparing outputs vs a golden baseline (semantic similarity, token-level divergence, hallucination indicators).
- Degradation event: fidelity drop or p95 latency breach after activation.

Compatibility matrix (example)
| Accelerator class | Min firmware | Supported quant formats | Expected max seq_len | Verified models (examples) | Notes |
|-------------------|--------------:|------------------------|----------------------:|---------------------------|-------|
| Remote NPU v1     | 2025-04-12    | int8, int8-with-scale   | 2048                 | Llama-2-13B, MPT-7B      | supports KV cache via proxy, 1.8x throughput gain |
| On-host A100-48GB | n/a           | fp16, bf16, int8        | 4096                 | Llama-2-70B              | native CUDA kernels, priority pinning required |
| ThirdParty-TPU    | 2024-12-01    | bfloat16                | 4096                 | Flan-T5-large            | network-attached, higher cold-start penalty |

Pre-integration checklist (must be completed before any staged traffic)
- [ ] Hardware and firmware versions recorded in the accelerator registry.
- [ ] Provider compatibility tested with the kernel mapper test harness.
- [ ] Baseline golden outputs produced using the canonical baseline environment (host-GPU fp16) for each target model and prompt set.
- [ ] Fidelity profile generation job configured and passing (see ‘Profiling and fidelity tests’).
- [ ] Scheduler policy authored: pool label, admission control thresholds, priority groups.
- [ ] Monitoring & alerting configured: fidelity-alert (>=3% semantic drop), latency-alert (p95 breach > configured SLOs).
- [ ] Rollout and rollback playbook drafted with owners identified.

Scheduler integration guidelines
- Resource classification: hybrid accelerators must be mapped to one of three scheduler resource classes: dedicated-accel, shared-accel, network-accel. Code-level tags: accel.class = {dedicated,shared,network}.
- Admission control signals: each pool exposes available_credits, max_concurrency, and warm_ratio (fraction of warmed KV sessions). Inject these into the request admission flow.
- Kernel hints: kernels must advertise fallback_compat set (list of compatible kernel variants) and deterministic_fallback_cost (approx ms). The scheduler consults fallback_compat before routing.
- Priority synthesis: combine request priority, SLO sensitivity, and customer tier to produce a scheduling key. For hybrid pool admission require: request_priority >= pool_min_priority and warm_ratio >= pool_min_warm.

Profiling and fidelity tests (playbook)
1) Canonical prompt set generation
   - Use the internal prompt-set-builder to produce 3 prompt cohorts: short-chat (<=128 tokens), multi-turn (3 turns, average 400 tokens), long-context (>=2048 tokens).
   - Save the seed corpus and store the job ID in the release ticket.

2) Golden baseline collection
   - Command (example):
     run-benchmark --model Llama-2-13B --backend host-gpu-fp16 --prompts prompts/llama13b-canonical.json --out baseline/llama13b-host-fp16.json

3) Accelerator run and raw trace capture
   - Command (example):
     run-benchmark --model Llama-2-13B --backend remote-npu-v1 --prompts prompts/llama13b-canonical.json --trace raw-traces/npu-v1/

4) Automated fidelity metrics job
   - Compare outputs with baseline and compute: ROUGE-L, BLEURT, token-level KL, and a semantic-similarity embedding score (cosine).
   - Thresholds (example):
     - Embedding cosine >= 0.92 vs baseline for short-chat cohort
     - BLEURT delta <= -0.03 for multi-turn cohort
     - No hallucination rate increase > 0.5% (see hallucination-detector v2)

5) Statistical significance and A/B harness
   - Run paired A/B for n >= 500 samples per cohort. If metrics are borderline, collect n >= 2000.

Benchmarking suite requirements
- Microbenchmarks: per-kernel latency histogram for 1..4096 sequence lengths, token throughput (tokens/s) under 1, 4, 16 concurrent sessions.
- End-to-end benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 for representative routes (completion, chat, embeddings).
- Cost model: estimate cost-per-token based on observed util and amortized kernel credits. Provide delta vs baseline.
- Energy estimate: if hardware monitoring available, include watt-seconds/token.

Release validation matrix
| Check | Pass criteria | Owner |
|-------|---------------|-------|
| Functional smoke | No errors on 100 sample requests | Release engineer |
| Fidelity | Embedding cosine >= 0.92 AND BLEURT delta within threshold | Profiling owner |
| Latency SLO | p95 <= configured SLO (route specific) | SRE |
| Stability | No OOMs, no kernel crashes for 24h soak | Kernel owner |
| Observability | Traces, metrics, and traces contain accel tags | Observability team |

Runbook: activate new accelerator pool (staged rollout)
1) Canary: enable pool for internal/beta customers only (5% of traffic). Monitor fidelity and latency in 1m buckets for 2 hours.
2) Expand: move to 20% if no alerts. Validate via A/B test comparing golden baseline metrics.
3) Ramp: move to 50% over 6-12 hours if rolling windows show steady state.
4) Full switch: 100% only after 48h of production stability and business sign-off.

Rollback gates and automated safety breakers
- Fidelity-alert: configured to trigger if embedding cosine drops by >= 0.03 on rolling 30-minute window across the canonical prompt set. Immediate automated action: pause routing to the accelerator pool and shift to fallback kernel for affected models.
- Latency SLO breach: if p95 breaches SLO for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows, reduce accelerator pool traffic by 50% automatically and notify SRE on-call.
- Crash circuit: 3 kernel crashes within 10 minutes triggers full evacuation and disables pool.

Investigation playbook (if degradation observed)
1) Capture failing requests using trace IDs from the fidelity job and store full KV state.
2) Re-run failing inputs locally against: baseline, accelerator variant, and deterministic fallback to compare token-by-token diffs. Use internal tool: fidelity-inspect --baseline baseline.json --variant variant.json --output diffs/
3) Check kernel telemetry: kernel-latency-distribution, kernel-mem-residency, and hardware-err logs.
4) If hardware fault suspected, quarantine node and escalate to hardware vendor with collected traces and firmware versions.

Kernel developer checklist for accelerator-targeted kernels
- Export deterministic_fallback_cost and fallback_compat metadata.
- Provide a regression harness (Docker image) that reproduces microbenchmark and includes a mock KV cache.
- Ensure deterministic seeding for ops that rely on RNG or beam search.
- Provide a smoke vector of at least 200 canonical prompts with expected output hashes.

Telemetry and dashboards (minimum required panels)
- Accelerator pool health: uptime, crash_count, avg_warm_ratio
- Fidelity rollup: embedding_cosine_rolling_30m, BLEURT_delta_30m, hallucination_rate_24h
- Cost & throughput: tokens/s, util_percent, estimated_cost_per_1M_tokens
- Observability traces: sample request traces with accel.* tags and kernel version metadata

Appendix A — Example scheduler policy snippet (YAML)
policy_name: \"npu-v1-weighted-pool\"
pool_label: \"remote-npu-v1\"
accel:
  class: network-accel
  max_concurrency: 64
  warm_ratio_threshold: 0.6
admission:
  min_priority: 20
  fallback_compat: [\"host-gpu-fp16\",\"on-host-a100-int8\"]

Appendix B — Common failure signatures and first actions
- High token-drop: look for quantization saturation (check kernel counter: q_saturation_rate). Action: reduce batch size and fall back.
- KV mismatch after warmstart: indicates proxy state desync. Action: flush session and force cold restart with warm hint disabled.
- Increased hallucination: compare hallucination_anchors and run hallucination-detector; run A/B with baseline.

Document maintenance and cadence
- This page is reviewed quarterly by the kernel integration guild.
- Any production incident that involves a hybrid accelerator must attach an incident note and suggested updates to this doc.
